walkthroughs.body_html:
Qualitative Research Methods (HL Extension) — a core area of Psychology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Qualitative Research Methods (HL Extension) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Qualitative Research Methods (HL Extension).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Braun and Clarke's 2006 thematic analysis has how many phases?
Reflecting on how the researcher shapes the data is called:
options: Triangulation
Reflexivity
Coding
Saturation

mcqs.q: In Pavlov's experiment, what is the conditioned response?
options: The dog ringing the bell itself.
Salivation to the food (which is automatic).
Salivation to the bell alone, after pairing with food.
Unlimited.

mcqs.q: What is the capacity of short-term memory according to Miller?
options: The dog ringing the bell itself.
Unlimited.
7 plus or minus 2 seconds.
7 plus or minus 2 items (chunks).

mcqs.q: How do SSRIs help with OCD?
options: They directly produce more serotonin in the brain.
Unlimited.
They prevent reabsorption of serotonin, increasing its availability in the synapse.
They block all neurotransmitters.
